requirements.title: A defined operation is interpreted by the function that defines it
requirements.definition: After a defined operation has been established under 10.1.6.1, its interpretation is the value and characteristics provided by the defining function, with operand-to-dummy correspondence supplied by the defined-operation interface rules.

pending.unary-operation-function-interpretation: PENDING source plan defining a unary operator function for a derived value and checking that op x has the same literal-bearing result as the defining function applied to x, without observing call order or number of calls.
pending.binary-operation-function-interpretation: PENDING source plan defining a binary operator function for derived operands and checking that x op y has the same component result as the function of x and y with left/right correspondence supplied by 15.4.3.4.2.
pending.direct-call-control: PENDING companion control that calls the same function directly with the same literal-bearing operands, establishing the expected value without compiler agreement or TRANSFER.
pending.no-intrinsic-fallback-for-applicable-def: PENDING intrinsic-symbol extension control where a derived operand route differs from intrinsic operations. The positive asserts only the defined function interpretation after applicability is established, not generic search details.

requirements.oracle: Future positives derive the expected result from the defining function semantics and literal operand components. They must not infer a call count, call order, short-circuit decision, or emitted implementation strategy.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This source-only catalogue records pending plans only. It creates no Fortran test program, invokes no processor, approves no fixture or oracle, and claims no coverage. Future cases must not infer which operand was evaluated, the order of evaluation, or whether an optional evaluation was omitted; must not assert a result that a permitted mathematically or logically equivalent rewrite could change; must not use floating-point tolerance as an escape hatch; must not rely on compiler agreement, address arithmetic, TRANSFER, emitted assembly, or undefined reads; and must attribute every negative to the cited requirement rather than to an independently invalid rule owned elsewhere.

requirements.title: Symbolic and named relational operator spellings have the same interpretations
requirements.definition: The relational operator pairs < and .LT., <= and .LE., > and .GT., >= and .GE., == and .EQ., and /= and .NE. always have the same interpretations respectively, including when a relational intrinsic-operator spelling is extended by a defined operation under the interface rules.

pending.symbolic-less-same-as-lt: PENDING paired positive controls using < and .LT. in otherwise identical relational contexts and comparing standard-defined results. Character controls, if used, must blank-pad the shorter operand under 10.1.5.5.2.
pending.symbolic-less-equal-same-as-le: PENDING paired positive controls using <= and .LE. with operands whose result is independent of permitted evaluation rewrites and kind conversion surprises.
pending.symbolic-greater-same-as-gt: PENDING paired positive controls using > and .GT.; any negative spelling or operand-type issue belongs to the grammar or 10.1.5 owner, not to this equivalence requirement.
pending.symbolic-greater-equal-same-as-ge: PENDING paired positive controls using >= and .GE. with fixed operands and a literal oracle for the common interpretation.
pending.symbolic-equal-same-as-eq: PENDING paired positive controls using == and .EQ. with operands chosen so equality interpretation is owned by 10.1.5 or an applicable defined operation, not by evaluation order.
pending.symbolic-not-equal-same-as-ne: PENDING paired positive controls using /= and .NE. with complementary literal oracle and no undefined operands.
pending.relational-defined-extension-paired-spel: PENDING OPERATOR relational extension control showing that extending one relational spelling supplies the paired spelling as described by 15.4.3.4.2 p3; generic interface validity and distinguishability remain dependencies.

requirements.oracle: Future controls compare paired spellings in matched contexts. Character relational controls must account for blank padding of the shorter operand; this requirement owns spelling equivalence, not character collation or relational operand validity.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This source-only catalogue records pending plans only. It creates no Fortran test program, invokes no processor, approves no fixture or oracle, and claims no coverage. Future cases must not infer which operand was evaluated, the order of evaluation, or whether an optional evaluation was omitted; must not assert a result that a permitted mathematically or logically equivalent rewrite could change; must not use floating-point tolerance as an escape hatch; must not rely on compiler agreement, address arithmetic, TRANSFER, emitted assembly, or undefined reads; and must attribute every negative to the cited requirement rather than to an independently invalid rule owned elsewhere.

review_rationale: batch103: independent fresh-context source review against pinned J3/24-007 (sha256 7371e889...). Reviewer read all 20 base units of 10.1.6.1, 10.1.6.2, 10.1.6.3, 10.1.7 and 10.1.8 in the original PDF rather than the author summary, verified 20 base / 56 fine units, 10 requirements and 63 facets (all pending), and separately re-read the 10.1.2.4, 10.1.2.6, 10.1.2.8 and 10.1.2.9 grammar units to confirm ownership. A global name-head check over 502 rule heads found 0 missing, 0 duplicate and 0 unmatched, and confirmed the defined-operator grammar owners remain R1004/C1005, R1024/C1006, R1012, R1020 and R1022. Every processor freedom is correctly recorded as a permission: 10.1.6.3 p1 equivalent-expression latitude is bounded by parenthesis integrity, 10.1.7 p1 records that a processor need not evaluate all operands or evaluate each entirely, and 10.1.8 p1 keeps the rewrite context as permission while preserving the normative requirement that a parenthesized expression be treated as a data entity. 10.1.7 p3 is the single restriction in scope, with its CRITICAL and END CRITICAL exceptions. This packet carries four delegations left open by earlier batches: defined-binary applicability and generic nonapplicability from 10.1.2.9, and the left-recursive grouping facets from 10.1.2.6 and 10.1.2.8, which are discharged through a value-observable non-associative defined extension rather than through truth tables, short-circuiting or side effects. Undefined-status effects are recorded as not value-observable by reading the entity, and finite samples are recorded as able to refute but never to prove the all-possible-primary-values equivalence of 10.1.6.3 p2. Decision: accept, no blocking findings; three non-blocking observations recorded in doc/source_audits/batch_103.json. This registers source accounting only: it is not fixture approval, it supplies no execution, and it approves no oracle.
